prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a downward-angled egocentric view over a brick floor that slopes in brightness from roughly 1.2–1.5 m directly below the camera wearer to over 2.5–3 m toward the top of each frame. The camera wearer's own striped chest (0.2–0.4 m away) and raised arms and hands (0.3–0.7 m away, within immediate self-reach) appear brightest at the bottom, while a standing person to the right holding a bottle against their torso is at an intermediate distance of about 1.0–1.5 m (just at or slightly beyond arm's reach) and a person on the left in white trousers is similarly 1.0–1.5 m away, making the two bystanders roughly 1.5–2.0 m apart from each other. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's left and right hands rise toward the camera in frames 2–3 (brightening as they come within 0.3–0.5 m and partially occluding the floor and parts of the nearby people) before lowering in frames 4–5 as the person on the left steps slightly closer into the bottom-left corner. This map makes the continuous vertical distance gradient from the wearer's upper torso down to their feet (~1.3 m below) and the exact 3D relief of the raised hands against the tilted brick ground much clearer than RGB alone. However, it looks unreliable in frames 2 and 3 where the steep downward floor gradient goes overly dark near the top edge, completely losing the distant feet (~2.5–3 m away) visible at the top-right of frames 1 and 2, and blurring the depth boundary between the wearer's lower legs and the floor.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels parts of three main people in the immediate scene (around 0.2–1.5 m from the camera) plus a fourth distant person's feet (~2.5–3 m away at the top-right of frame 2) and a small handheld water bottle (~1.2 m away on the right). In frames 1 and 3, it isolates the green-capped bottle held within the right-hand bystander's grasp against their dark clothing, which is small and low-contrast in the RGB view, while also tracking the cropped legs of the person to the left (1.0–1.5 m away) and the person to the right (1.0–1.5 m away), both of whom stand facing roughly forward/inward alongside the camera wearer with their heads out of view or looking down rather than toward the camera. Across frames 2 to 5, the camera wearer's raised arms and torso (0.2–0.7 m away at the bottom) sweep up and down in front of the lens, partially occluding the floor and touching the mask boundaries of the surrounding people. However, the map is highly unreliable in instance consistency and object classification: it completely misses the camera wearer's torso in frame 1, fragments the wearer's own body and limbs into two or three separate 'person' instances across frames 2–5, merges the wearer's right arm with the bystander on the right in frames 2 and 5, and mislabels the left bystander's shoe in frame 2 as a 'remote'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D skeletons on a black background, capturing only the person standing ~1.0–1.5 m to the right in frame 1 (facing leftward/inward with head tilted down away from the camera, left hand holding the bottle at waist level within their own reach, and legs extending down to the floor) and one of the camera wearer's own hands (~0.3–0.6 m in front of and below the lens) in frames 2 through 5. Across the sequence, the magenta hand skeleton tracks the camera wearer's left hand spreading its fingers in frame 2, the right hand curling in frame 3 as the left arm exits the left edge, the left hand spreading again in frame 4, and the left hand flexing downward in frame 5, while a partial yellow leg skeleton briefly appears on the wearer's lower body (~1.2 m below the camera) in frame 2. The magenta keypoints make the fine finger articulation and palm orientation of the wearer's active hand (facing away from the camera in frames 2, 4, and 5, and angled inward in frame 3) easier to read than against the busy brick texture in RGB. However, the pose estimator is largely unreliable for scene-wide layout because heavy top-down perspective foreshortening and partial framing cause it to miss the camera wearer's torso and second arm in every frame, miss the right-side bystander entirely in frames 2–5, and fail to detect the cropped person on the left (~1.0–1.5 m away) or the distant walker (~2.5–3 m away) in any frame.
